<thought>We have determined from the mass spectrum that the molecular ion is at m/z ≈ 199 with a significant M+2 peak, indicating one chlorine atom (Cl contributes ~35.45 Da, and the isotopic pattern matches Cl). The ¹H NMR shows two aromatic doublets (2 H each) around 7.2–7.4 ppm, consistent with a para‑substituted phenyl ring, and two aliphatic triplets (2 H each) at 2.6–2.8 ppm, indicating a –CH₂CH₂– chain attached to the aromatic ring. The ¹³C NMR shows eight distinct carbons: six aromatic carbons (including two sets of equivalent carbons) and two aliphatic carbons at ~43 ppm and ~39 ppm, matching a phenyl‑CH₂‑CH₂‑Cl fragment. The formula consistent with these data is C₈H₉Cl (monoisotopic mass ≈ 198.99 Da). The structure that fits all observations is 1‑chloro‑2‑phenylethane, whose SMILES is “ClCCc1ccccc1”.</thought>
<final_answer>ClCCc1ccccc1</final_answer>
